source_artifacts.claim: Pac holds OPEN to open Isp patrol gate. Isp crosses raised refuges, avoiding the rolling bomb. Rescue latch near right opens both patrol/exit gates and powers refuge_two; Isp reaches its exit, Pac traverses to orange exit. refuge_two is safe only during powered pause (3s per 10s cycle); route must respect it. Two owner collectibles optional.
Overlapping an active harmful hazard sets the level state to dead.
Retry recreates the level state and clears input, returning both heroes to their authored starts.

isp: Use the raised refuges to cross above Gem's rolling bomb while Pac holds OPEN.
Wait at refuge_one for refuge_two's three-second safe pause in its ten-second cycle, then latch RESCUE.
Reach Isp's matching exit; RESCUE also opens Pac's exit gate.
pac: Hold OPEN so Isp can cross the patrol gate to the refuges and RESCUE pad.
After RESCUE opens Pac's gate, cross the floor to Pac's matching exit while avoiding the rolling bomb.

common_mistakes.mistake: Isp leaves refuge_one and attempts refuge_two outside its three-second safe pause, dropping into the rolling-bomb path; a separate reversible error is simply waiting through the moving part of the cycle.
common_mistakes.consequence: Missing the pause without contact costs time and can be retried from refuge_one. If the rolling bomb overlaps Isp, the authored hazard marks the level dead; that is a lethal reset, not a missed-cycle wait.
common_mistakes.recovery: For a missed cycle, return to or remain on refuge_one and cross during the next safe pause. After bomb death, press R; the runtime recreates the level at both start positions, so Pac must reopen the patrol route and Isp must repeat the crossing and RESCUE. No such mistake recovery was observed in current44.

incorrect_inferences: The “timed or changing condition” was right but not enough; the timed pause is a meaningful crossing window, not merely an idle uncertainty.
changed_judgments: Timing/execution/hazard/recovery scored from authored motion and successful historical input, not human performance; reasoning/cooperation stay modest because one pad-to-rescue sequence is straightforward.

single_operator_note: Baseline assessment assumes two humans on the shared keyboard. One operator would need to switch between role key sets and coordinate simultaneous pad/target states; no operator comparison was performed.
